BiblicalUsage: Chimham is an Israelite who crosses the Jordan in David's place. 2 Samuel 19:37 has Barzillai asking David to let his servant Chimham go over with the king instead of him, and 2 Samuel 19:38 has David answering, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee. Jeremiah 41:17 remembers him still, in the habitation of Chimham by Bethlehem, where the fugitives stopped on their way to Egypt.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Chimham is the picture of a faithful servant carried by another man's loyalty: Barzillai's gift became David's companion, and his name outlived them both beside Bethlehem.
